subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Flow Rate and Continuity
description: A quick, practical guide to Flow Rate and Continuity.

hook.text: Pinch a garden hose and the water shoots faster. Why?

buildup.text: Flow rate is volume per second. What enters a pipe must leave it.

discovery.text: Shrink the area and the speed must rise to keep flow rate constant.

twist.text: This works in reverse too. Widen a pipe and the flow slows down.

climax.text: Blood vessels use this: arteries narrow to speed blood to organs.

punchline.text: Narrow the path and the fluid hurries through.

quiz.question: Why does fluid speed up when a pipe narrows?
options: Pressure forces the fluid to accelerate through the gap
The same volume must pass a smaller area, so velocity increases
Friction in the narrow section pushes the fluid faster
